key_insight: PQuantML is an open-source, hardware-aware library that unifies pruning and fixed-point quantization into an end-to-end workflow, enabling practitioners to compress models (jointly or separately) while accounting for real latency constraints on target hardware.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between model compression research and deployment by providing a single, easy-to-use tool that produces low-latency, resource-efficient models suitable for constrained or latency-sensitive hardware environments.
method: Unified API to apply pruning and fixed-point quantization either jointly or independently within a single training/deployment pipeline.
Implements multiple pruning granularities (e.g., weight-, channel-, and layer-level) so users can trade off sparsity patterns and performance.
Hardware-aware optimization that factors device constraints into compression decisions to maintain accuracy while meeting latency/resource budgets.
impact: Makes it faster and safer for ML engineers to produce deployment-ready, compressed models for edge and embedded targets, reducing iteration time and unexpected performance regressions on real hardware.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data/model → pruning → quantization → hardware-aware profiler → deployed model (shows unified end-to-end flow)
Tradeoff chart: accuracy vs latency/size for baseline vs pruning-only vs quantization-only vs joint compression
Granularity illustration: schematic showing weight-, channel-, and layer-level pruning effects on a CNN block
Icons: open-source repo, chip/edge device, speedometer (latency), and accuracy shield
paper_title: PQuantML: A Tool for End-to-End Hardware-aware Model Compression
paper_authors: Roope Niemi, Anastasiia Petrovych, Arghya Ranjan Das, Enrico Lupi, Chang Sun
